methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Arc Boats is a Series B-stage transportation company that has raised $100M+ to date. The relevant peer universe consists of eight private frontier-tech transportation firms, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Parallel Systems, and The ePlane Company. No public transportation comparables exist at sufficient scale or stage proximity to support benchmarking.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a proxy for pre-money valuation at Series B entry, a 1.9x step-up multiplier—consistent with typical Series B-to-Series C progression—yields an implied valuation of $190M. This method assumes Arc Boats' capital efficiency and risk profile align with median frontier-tech advancement rates. A peer-median approach was not viable; while three transportation-sector companies exist in the broader comp set, none share identical stage, adjacent-stage proximity, or valuation-tier alignment required for reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median point of $190M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than high conviction across triangulated approaches. Key uncertainties include Arc Boats' actual pre-money valuation at Series B close, capital efficiency relative to frontier-tech norms, and whether the 1.9x multiplier appropriately reflects current market conditions for deep-tech transportation businesses. Additional data on comparable Series B outcomes in this sector would strengthen conviction in this range.
